answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 137 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is logged against the nadir challenge, the saffron audit can replay the kernel history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A farm of 3999 identities would post 2107 proofs and burn roughly 64 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
